$comment: HAND-WRITTEN, AND READ BY BOTH PLATOOLS SDKS. WIN-270 (M4.4), cross-language fixtures.
packages/platools-js/tests/protocol-fixture.test.ts (vitest) and
packages/platools-py/tests/test_protocol_fixture.py (pytest) each declare the tool below in
their own language, drive their own PlatoolsClient through registration and dispatch, and
compare the FRAMES IT PUTS ON THE WIRE against this file. Two SDKs that disagree about a key,
a type, a default or an error string cannot both match one fixture.
The frame key sets are also joined to the platform: both suites parse the protocol header of
apps/agent/src/tool-gateway/tool-sync-ws.service.ts and require `keys` below to equal what the
server documents, so this file cannot drift away from the consumer the frames are written for.
A key ending in `?` is optional there and may be absent or null on the wire.
`tool.parameters` is the JSON-Schema MEANING both SDKs must derive, not their spelling: zod and
pydantic decorate a schema differently (titles, `anyOf` vs a type array), so each suite reads its
own `input_schema` as, per property in declaration order, the set of JSON types it admits
(`type` string or array, plus every `anyOf` member's type), whether it is required, and its
`default` when one is present and not null. A null default on a nullable optional parameter
states nothing an absent default does not.
The handler both suites register returns
{ received: { order_id, quantity, gift }, scope: { organizationId, projectId, environmentId } }
with `scope` read from the SDK's own current-scope accessor, so the expected `tool_result` proves
the `__platos` envelope reached the call context, the `_context` and `__platos` envelopes never
reached the handler's arguments, and the declared default for `gift` was applied.

tool.name: lookup_order
tool.description: Look up one order by id.
